title: Trio SDK: credential-fallback controller, adaptive heartbeat & streamed wrapper parity
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: teams using all three SDKs reported brittle auth handoffs during long-lived streams and incompatible generator/async-iterator ergonomics across Python/TS/Go. This PR introduces a small, backward-compatible controller that orchestrates credential fallback (fanout) + an adaptive heartbeat window to reduce noisy reauths, plus a thin streamed-wrapper that normalizes generator/async-iterable surface area across languages. High-level changes: 1) credential-fallback controller (typed, pluggable backends) that prefers local cache -> delegated refresh -> fallback proxy; 2) heartbeat window with adaptive jitter and soft-throttle to avoid synchronized reauth storms; 3) streamed-wrapper that exposes a consistent async iterator / generator-friendly API and improves backpressure hooks; 4) docs and examples for cross-language patterns and an incremental TS SDK minor version bump. Compatibility: default behavior preserves existing user flows; opt-in via new ClientOptions fields documented in CHANGELOG. Checklist: [x] design review, [x] unit tests for controller logic, [x] cross-SDK integration smoke tests with Python/Go teams, [x] documentation and examples, [x] version bump and changelog. Testing: local integration with example service, CI matrix across node 16/18, run python/Go smoke jobs in CI orchestration. Rollback plan: revert feature flag and strip controller registration; no runtime breaking changes expected. Notes on parity: Python generator examples included in docs/interop.md; Go SDK team agreed minor API alias to reduce churn. Release impact: TS v1.28.1, compatibility shim for v1.27.x users documented.

review_conversation: Jonah Kim (reviewer): Please confirm the fallback order and surface area for custom credential providers; we should allow users to register a priority list. Reply: Asha: Controller accepts a prioritized list and exposes registerFallback(provider, priority). Added tests for ordering.

Priya Desai (reviewer): Heartbeat jitter math looks aggressive for 1000+ concurrent streams; can we make defaults conservative? Reply: Asha: lowered default jitter scale and added an env flag REDWOOD_HEARTBEAT_SCALE for experiments; documented tradeoffs.

Luca Romano (reviewer): Small nit: streamedWrapper exposes close() vs return(); prefer consistent naming across SDKs. Reply: Asha: renamed to close() and added an alias return() for backward compat; updated Python/Go examples to call close().
CI (automated): smoke-python job failed on first run due to missing py-smoke matrix entry. Asha: fixed CI matrix and re-ran; subsequent run passed.
release_notes: Introduced credential-fallback controller (pluggable order), adaptive heartbeat window to reduce auth churn, and a streamed-wrapper that normalizes async iterator/generator ergonomics across SDKs. TS package bumped to 1.28.1. Opt-in via ClientOptions. See docs/interop.md for migration guidance.
notes: This PR coordinates with python (#pr to be opened by python SDK lead) and go SDK teams; follow-up tasks tracked in ENG-4187 for metrics gating and rollout of heartbeat defaults. Observability: new metrics auth.fallback.* and heartbeat.window_ms to be exposed to Console.
